turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Meredith stops just inside the door and doesn't sit. She sets a slim folder on the nearest desk.

"Meredith Kalinowski. I have until half past four.

My son found out about this from the online gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me first.

So let's start with who decided, when, and on what basis."
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I know your schedule is brutal.

"Then you'll understand why I'd like an answer to my question.

Who decided, when, and on what basis?"

She doesn't open the folder yet.
I have to say, you're far more reasonable than I expected. Most parents come in swinging.

"I haven't been reasonable yet. I've asked a question, and you haven't answered it.

'Most parents come in swinging.' Is that how this file is being read? Parents who object are swingers, and the zero stands?"

She finally opens the folder and takes out a single sheet.

"Who decided, Hale? Was it you, or the software?"
It's refreshing. You clearly see the whole picture, so I think we're really on the same side here.

"We're not on the same side. You gave my son a zero. I'm here to find out why.

'On the same side.' If that's true, it'll be easy to answer three things. Who made the decision. What it was based on. And was Owen asked a single question before his mark changed?"

She sets the sheet down, squared to the edge of the desk.

"I'll want the answers in an email. Start with the first one."
